blocks.text: I can recognise the future tense and the conditional of -er verbs in a range of texts about places to live.
Tap the word to see what it means.

items.def: a form of verb used to express what would happen

blocks.text: ‘Les logements’ means accommodation. Here are some words for the rooms and things inside.
The 1-verb future says what will happen. Regular -er verbs use the infinitive as the stem plus the future endings {-ai}, {-as}, {-a}, {-ons}, {-ez}, {-ont}.
There is no separate word for ‘will’: the spelling of the verb contains the future meaning.
Listen for three sounds: [i] as in ‘midi’, [on] as in ‘non’ and [ez] as in ‘nez’. The plural future endings have the sounds [ez] and [on]: parlerons, parlerez, parleront.
-s and -t are silent at the end of a word, so ‘parlerons’ and ‘parleront’ sound the same. Most future endings (ai, as, a, ont) are ‘avoir’ in the present tense, which makes them easier to remember.

items.q: vous ___ (chercher: you plural will look for)
elle ___ (surveiller: she will keep an eye on)

blocks.text: The conditional says what would happen. Regular -er verbs use the infinitive as the stem plus the imperfect endings {-ais}, {-ais}, {-ait}, {-ions}, {-iez}, {-aient}.
There is no separate word for ‘would’ either. The verb’s spelling contains the full conditional meaning.
The ‘nous’ and ‘vous’ conditional forms have the sound [i] (parlerions, parleriez). That makes them sound different from the future forms.
Be careful: ‘ais’, ‘ait’ and ‘aient’ sound the same. The silent final consonants come after -ai, so they all sound like [è].
So je chercherais, tu chercherais, on chercherait and elles chercheraient all sound the same. Pay close attention to the subject of the verb to know which spelling to use.

blocks.q: Which pronoun fits the conditional verb?
Is each verb in the 1-verb future (will) or the conditional (would)?

blocks.text: Use ‘soit … soit’ to mean ‘either … or’. Place ‘soit’ before each alternative.

items: J’habiterai soit en ville, soit à la campagne = I will live either in town or in the countryside.
Vous achèterez soit une maison, soit un appartement = You will buy either a house or a flat.
Ils habiteront soit au Royaume-Uni, soit en Corse = They will live either in the United Kingdom or in Corsica.

blocks.text: These words come from a blog about where people will live in the future. Tap a word to see its meaning.

blocks.q: Match the French words to their English meanings.

blocks.text: Sam writes: ‘Un jour, j’aimerais habiter dans un appartement de quatre chambres sur la côte en Corse.’

blocks.q: Where would Sam like to live?
options: a 4-bedroom house near a British beach
a 4-bedroom flat on the coast in Corsica
a 4-bedroom flat far from the beach
blocks.why: ‘Un appartement de quatre chambres sur la côte en Corse’ is a four-bedroom flat on the coast in Corsica.

blocks.text: Alex writes: ‘Moi, je voudrais vivre près d’un lac, à la campagne, pour bénéficier de la nature.’

blocks.q: Where would Alex like to live?
options: near a lake in the countryside
in the middle of the traffic
blocks.why: ‘Près d’un lac, à la campagne’ means near a lake, in the countryside.

blocks.q: In the blog: ‘Certains apprécieront la vie urbaine.’ What does ‘apprécieront’ mean?
blocks.why: The ending -ont is a 1-verb future ending, so apprécieront means ‘they will appreciate’.

blocks.q: In the blog: ‘…elles adapteraient leurs maisons…’ What does ‘adapteraient’ mean?
blocks.why: The ending -aient is a conditional ending (the imperfect endings on the infinitive stem), so adapteraient means ‘they would adapt’.

items: [i] is pronounced as in ‘midi’, [on] as in ‘non’ and [ez] as in ‘nez’.
The 1-verb future of -er verbs: add -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont to the infinitive.
The conditional uses the same stem as the 1-verb future (the infinitive).
The conditional endings are the same as the imperfect: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.

worksheet.instructions: Write your answers in French unless the question asks for English. Include the pronoun shown in the question, and check your accents.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the 1-verb future of habiter: ‘we (plural) will live’.
Write in French, using the 1-verb future of décider: ‘they (mixed) will decide’.
Write in French, using the 1-verb future of chercher: ‘you (plural) will look for’.
Write in French, using the conditional of écouter: ‘he would listen’.
questions.explanation: écouter + the imperfect ending -ait gives il écouterait.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the conditional of danser: ‘we (plural) would dance’.
questions.explanation: danser + the imperfect ending -ions gives nous danserions.

questions.prompt: Write in French, using the conditional of chercher: ‘you (plural) would look for’.
questions.explanation: chercher + the imperfect ending -iez gives vous chercheriez.

questions.prompt: The conditional endings are the same as the endings of which tense? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: The conditional endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient are the imperfect endings.
